items.abstract: <jats:p>Machine learning based network intrusion detection systems (NIDS) consistently demonstrate excellent detection performance on benchmark datasets such as CICIDS2017. However, their performance often degrades when they are deployed in different network environments because the statistical characteristics of network traffic vary across datasets. This study investigates the impact of domain shift on the cross dataset generalization of machine learning based intrusion detection models. Cross dataset experiments were conducted using the CICIDS2017 dataset and a self-generated dataset collected from a controlled enterprise like virtual testbed, where models were trained on one dataset and evaluated on the other. The results show a substantial reduction in detection performance under cross dataset evaluation, indicating that models mainly learn dataset specific patterns rather than general network attack characteristics. The experiments also showed that the transferability between the two datasets was not symmetric. Models trained on the self-generated dataset adapted better to CICIDS2017 than models trained on CICIDS2017 adapted to the self-generated dataset. To better understand this behaviour, the distribution differences between the two datasets were examined using four statistical measures: the Kolmogorov Smirnov (KS) statistic, Wasserstein Distance (WD), Jensen Shannon (JS) Divergence, and Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD). The analysis indicates that differences in feature distributions, traffic behaviour, and class characteristics play an important role in the observed decline in cross dataset performance. Among all features, flow duration, inter arrival time, and packet length related features show the largest distributional differences between the two datasets. These findings show that high within dataset accuracy does not necessarily translate into strong cross dataset generalization. They also highlight the importance of evaluating intrusion detection systems using data collected from different network environments.</jats:p>
title: Quantifying Domain Shift in DDoS Intrusion Detection: A Cross dataset Evaluation Using CICIDS2017 and a Controlled Testbed Dataset

items.abstract: <jats:p>Intrusion detection systems are used to detect attacks in a network.  Machine learning (ML) approaches have been widely used to build such Intrusion Detection Systems (IDSs) because they are more accurate when built from a very large and representative dataset. In recent times, one of the benchmark datasets that are used to build ML-based Intrusion Detection models is CICIDS2017 dataset. The dataset is contained in eight groups and was collected from the Canadian Institute on Cyber Security dataset repository.  The dataset is available in both PCAP and netflow formats. This study used the netflow records in the CIDIDS2017 dataset as they are found to contain newer attacks,very large and are found useful for traffic analysis. Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) techniques were used to reveal various characteristics of the dataset. The general objective is to provide more insights on the nature, structure and issues with the dataset so as  to identify the best ways for using it to achieve improved ML-based IDS models. Furthermore, some of the open problems that can arise from the use of the dataset in any machine learning-based Intrusion Detection systems are highlighted and possible solutions are briefly discussed. The EDA techniques used revealed important relationships among input variables and the target class. The study concluded that the EDA can better influence the decision of future IDS researches that use the dataset. Thus, improved machine learning-based intrusion detection systems can be built from the dataset once it is well understood and pre-processed.</jats:p>
title: Overview and Exploratory Analyses of CICIDS2017 Intrusion Detection Dataset
